subject: English
description: Grammar + idiom + structure errors, plus trickier subject-verb cases

questions.stem: Spot the error: 'She has been living here (A) / since three years (B) / and is very happy (C) / with her neighbours. (D)'
questions.explanation: 'Since' + a point in time (since 2020). For a duration, use 'FOR'. Correct: 'for three years' (not 'since three years').
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Spot the error: 'The furniture in my office (A) / are new (B) / and very (C) / comfortable. (D)'
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is an UNCOUNTABLE noun — takes singular verb. 'The furniture IS new' (not 'are'). Similar: luggage, information, advice, news.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Spot the error: 'One of the boys (A) / are absent (B) / today due to (C) / illness. (D)'
questions.explanation: 'One of + plural noun' takes SINGULAR verb. 'One of the boys IS absent today' (not 'are'). Similarly: 'Each of the boys is...' / 'Neither of the boys is...'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Spot the error: 'He is senior (A) / than me (B) / by ten years (C) / of experience. (D)'
questions.explanation: Latin-origin adjectives ending in -ior take 'TO', not 'THAN'. Correct: 'senior TO me'. Similar: junior, superior, inferior, prior, posterior — all take 'to'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Spot the error: 'The chairman along with (A) / his team members (B) / were invited (C) / to the meeting. (D)'
questions.explanation: 'A along with B' takes a verb agreeing with A (the principal subject). Chairman is singular → 'WAS invited'. 'Together with / as well as / accompanied by' follow the same rule — they do NOT make the subject plural.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Spot the error: 'If I would have (A) / known about it, (B) / I would have (C) / helped you. (D)'
questions.explanation: 3rd conditional: 'If + past perfect, would have + V3'. 'If I HAD known... I would have helped...'. Never 'if + would have' in the IF-clause.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Spot the error: 'The committee (A) / have decided (B) / to release the (C) / funds next week. (D)'
questions.explanation: 'Committee' is a COLLECTIVE NOUN. When the group is treated as a single unit (and verb in Indian English usually takes singular), use 'HAS'. 'The committee has decided...' (British English sometimes allows plural when emphasising individual members, but the exam-standard form is singular.)
questions.subject: English
